# Voice guide

A reviewer has not approved this file.

Status: Draft.

This guide is for the strings in the copy deck. It does not change the app. Sound and haptic cues stay in the motion spec. This guide does not restate them.

## Tone

Write plain, warm, grade 7 English. Speak to the learner as a person.

Do not use a village riddle. Do not scold. Do not boast.

Warmth sits in the meaning. The learner is welcome. The next step is small and clear. A puzzle is not warmth. A scold is not clarity. A boast is not proof.

A button starts with a verb. "I said it" is the one label that opens with "I". It reports the act, and the verb in the line is "said". The Profile button ships as "Open all features", which starts with a verb.

Do not use an em dash in a string that ships.

ELEVATION.md section 3.4 names three boast words. Do not use them. This file does not repeat them.

Do not use an emoji as an icon. Use a word.

Do not use a confidence number. Do not use a percent sign. Do not use a points total.

If a line is over grade 7, do not ship it. The copy deck shows the formula, the score, and the fix.

## Do and do not

Each pair is one real moment in this app.

### 1. Onboarding

Do: "Why are you learning this language?"

Do not: "Who are you, and why do you seek knowledge?"

The old line is a riddle. The new line asks for a reason. The birth year is its own question: "What year were you born?" The speaking step asks "Can you say this greeting out loud?" It does not ask how the learner learns best.

### 2. A wrong answer

Do: "The check is unsure. Say the word again in a quiet place."

Do not: "Wrong." Do not show a score or a confidence number, and do not use a percent sign.

The check says what it heard, then gives the next step. It does not blame the learner.

### 3. Offline

Do: "The phone has no network. This plan is not saved on the phone. Connect, then try again."

Do not: "You should have saved this." Do not blame the learner for the missing network.

Say what failed, why this screen cannot open, and the next step.

### 4. AI unavailable

Do: "No reply came back. The tutor cannot answer right now. Try again later. Polie did not speak for you."

Do not: write the learner's line for them. Do not say Polie answered.

The tutor did not speak for the learner. Polie is the tutor. The last sentence says that in the words the learner sees.

### 5. A locked lesson

Do: "Morning greetings comes first." Offer "See a preview" and "Open the locked lesson".

Do not: "You are not ready." Do not scold.

The lesson can still open. The line names what comes first.

### 6. A celebration

Do: "The lesson is complete. You said the greeting."

Do not: "You did it!" Do not add a points total, a percent, or a rank.

The line names the fact. Lesson complete and level up are the only celebrations. This guide does not describe their sound or their haptic.

### 7. A microphone

Do: "Hold to talk." While it is open: "Polie is listening to you." and "You are talking." Then "Stop."

Do not: open the mic before the learner holds. Do not scold a quiet room.

The learner starts the turn and ends it.

### 8. A first spoken word

Do: "You speak now." Then, for the one syllable: "It was mid. The high tone sits up."

Do not: "You did it!" Do not show how close the tone was as a number.

"Speak within 60 seconds" is a target. The next line says "This is a target, not a timer." No account is required yet.

### 9. A save prompt

Do: "Save your progress?" Then: "You finished the first lesson. An account keeps it if you change phones."

Do not: "Save your progress and your streak." Do not say the lesson will vanish if they wait.

If they wait, the line is "Your answers stay on this phone." The button is "Skip for now".

### 10. A notification ask

Do: "Want a nudge at the time you practised today?"

Do not: "A soft nudge when it matters." Do not guilt the learner. Do not use a flame icon, or any emoji, as the icon.

The time is the learner's own practice time. It is not a clock this guide invents.

## Error copy

Use three lines, in this order.

1. What happened.
2. Why.
3. What to do.

Keep each line short. Name the thing that failed. Name the reason this screen cannot go on. Name one next step. Do not boast about the recovery.

### Load failure

What happened: "The plan did not open."

Why: "The lesson list did not come back."

What to do: "Try again."

### Offline

What happened: "The phone has no network."

Why: "This plan is not saved on the phone."

What to do: "Connect, then try again."

### AI unavailable

What happened: "No reply came back."

Why: "The tutor cannot answer right now."

What to do: "Try again later. Polie did not speak for you."

The tutor did not speak for the learner. Do not fill the silence with a line the learner did not say.
